name: Serine
info: The hydroxyl group forms hydrogen bonds and can be phosphorylated.

history.clue: The name comes from the Latin word for “silk.”
history.story: In 1865, Emil Cramer first obtained serine from silk protein. This is the origin of the name: the Latin sericum means “silk.” The source from which it was isolated became the name of an amino acid that is also found in many other proteins.
